title: Semantic-constrained glyph reconciliation experiment

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Accepted architecture, preservation boundary, pass criteria, and hard stop rule.

expectedLearning: Whether the same semantic-constrained matcher and bounded geometry scheduler cover all four adversarial cases without bespoke scheduling.
Whether the replacement preserves KP interaction and accessibility while measurably reducing scheduling policy.
allowedWork: Evolve the existing durable animation artifact only with renderer-independent presentation constraints and backend capability requirements.
Implement one semantic-lineage adapter, one matcher, one geometry scheduler, one conservative fallback, one ephemeral plan, one JavaScript backend seam, and one headless backend.
Integrate exactly four cases: solve-x one-to-one, numerator or fraction merge with Cloze, quadratic plus-minus branching, and one crowded quadratic interval at wide and phone widths.
Add stable visual, collision, occlusion, performance, payload, architecture, browser, accessibility, and Theseus evidence; delete or reduce replaced scheduling policy.
disallowedWork: No operation-specific, quadratic-specific, fraction-specific, branch-specific, or viewport-specific scheduler and no new exception taxonomy.
No durable glyph IR, separate branch/card/backend artifact, second semantic animation format, or renderer-owned semantic identity.

No full Manim export, Python runtime, video encoding, CAS, live LLM API, dynamic package loading, another renderer family, radical handoff repair, quadratic publication, family rollout, curriculum expansion, or unrelated roadmap work.
goal: Determine whether one semantic-lineage-constrained matcher and one bounded geometry scheduler can cover four adversarial animation cases while preserving KP interaction and reducing scheduling complexity; otherwise stop custom-planner investment.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with its Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: H1 FIRST-EXEMPLAR: produce and verify slice-14 evidence before cases 2-4; stop only if it triggers another named failure.
H2 FINAL-DECISION: stop at slice 24 for explicit PASS or STOP_CUSTOM_PLANNER review.
H3 BESPOKE-SCHEDULING: stop if any case needs operation-, family-, branch-, or viewport-specific scheduling.
H4 AMBIGUITY: stop if matching must infer semantic lineage from glyph equality or silently choose a plausible lineage.
H5 LAYERING: stop if measured glyphs, backend plans, DOM handles, or renderer resources must enter the durable artifact.
H6 PRESERVATION: stop on exact math, lineage, multiplicity, branch, graph, card, Cloze, accessibility, review, route, seek, rewind, native settlement, or baseline regression.
H7 COMPLEXITY: stop if scheduling-policy sites or operation-specific modes increase or no old common-path policy can be deleted or reduced.
H8 PERFORMANCE: stop if budgets require case-specific optimization, silent feature lowering, or relaxed interaction targets.
H9 RADICAL-ISOLATION: stop if the experiment modifies or relies on the radical WebGL handoff residual.
H10 SCOPE: stop before full Manim export, another renderer or domain, Workbench publication, curriculum expansion, live LLM integration, CAS work, or broad style redesign.
H11 USER-OVERLAP: stop if required work cannot be separated from unrelated user-authored worktree changes.
H12 VERIFICATION: stop if a required gate fails without one bounded common-algorithm correction.

slices.title: Experiment-ledger
slices.summary: Frozen four canonical cases, fixed budgets, seven-file and ten-reference policy baseline, and explicit pass/fail rubric with focused tests.

slices.title: Negative-and-ambiguity-fixtures
slices.summary: Encoded equal-glyph non-lineage, repeated-token ambiguity, unsupported relation fallback, and crowded wide/phone overlap fixtures with nine focused tests.

slices.title: Durable-artifact-boundary
slices.summary: Added backward-compatible renderer-independent presentation constraints and capability requirements to AnimationAsset, with strict serialization boundaries and 14 focused tests.

slices.title: Canonical-executor-lineage-adapter
slices.summary: Projected canonical executor lineage into immutable glyph-blind reconciliation groups with explicit authority and multiplicity; invalid competing lineage is rejected.

slices.title: Ephemeral-reconciliation-plan
slices.summary: Added an immutable renderer-session reconciliation plan outside the durable asset, initialized solely from canonical lineage and shared presentation constraints.

slices.title: Lineage-constrained-matcher
slices.summary: Added a glyph matcher that admits candidates only within canonical lineage, leaves equal unconnected glyphs unmatched, and reports repeated-token ambiguity.

slices.title: Multiplicity-reconciliation
slices.summary: Represented merges and splits as explicit semantic group reconciliations while retaining unique within-group glyph matches and ambiguity evidence.

slices.title: Ambiguity-and-conservative-fallback
slices.summary: Resolved match results conservatively: ambiguity settles a whole semantic group, multiplicity reconciles as a group, and unsupported or unmatched mappings cut at semantic checkpoints.

slices.title: Native-notation-measurement-protocol
slices.summary: Added a backend-neutral settled native-notation measurement protocol covering bounds, protected regions, and style fingerprints while preserving semantic identity.

slices.title: Bounded-clearance-scheduler
slices.summary: Added one bounded geometry scheduler with direct paths, shortest clear top or bottom lanes, honest settlement, fixed budget enforcement, and no operation-specific policy.

slices.title: Headless-test-backend
slices.summary: Added a deterministic no-browser notation measurement backend with fixed metrics, protected regions, settlement epoch, and strict missing or duplicate metric rejection.

slices.title: JavaScript-renderer-seam
slices.summary: Added dependency-free static-JS playback with deterministic polyline sampling, direct seek and rewind, explicit settle crossfade, and strict host binding.

slices.title: Simple-solve-x-exemplar
slices.summary: Routed canonical solve-x x-persistence through one shared compiler from executor lineage to matcher, measurement, plan, clearance schedule, and deterministic static-JS playback without changing settled identity.

slices.title: First-human-exemplar-evidence
slices.summary: Added a live baseline/new solve-x review route with shared scrub/play/rewind controls, standard review inbox, planner evidence, responsive layout, and deterministic 10-frame wide/phone capture command. User pre-authorized continuation to remaining cases.

slices.title: Many-to-one-fraction-merge
slices.summary: Routed the canonical two-denominator fan-in through generic multiplicity matching and constituent scheduling; both source glyphs converge on one native target with no fraction-specific scheduling.

slices.title: Cloze-projection-on-merge
slices.summary: Projected a Cloze from the settled canonical merged-denominator selector with exact transform provenance and no transient glyph, measurement, or pixel authority.
